subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured JSON output requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@asterhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured JSON output requirements

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so the team has a clean shared view and a set of concrete next steps. I tried to capture pain, current stack, success criteria, and immediate asks around tool/function calling and structured outputs. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points
- Responses from current assistant are inconsistent when asked to perform actions (invoke APIs / step logic) — sometimes free text, sometimes pseudo-JSON.
- Downstream systems (billing, order platform) require deterministic, schema-compliant payloads for automated processing.
- Hard to audit which tool was actually called (no consistent function/tool call logs).

Current stack (what you told us)
- Hosting: AWS (EKS + ECS for microservices).
- Retrieval: internal RAG using OpenSearch; prompt orchestration via a homegrown layer.
- Orchestration: a lightweight orchestrator that expects a JSON REST payload {"action":..., "args":...} to trigger downstream workflows.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- Structured output: model responses must be strict JSON conforming to a provided schema, with >=95% pass rate on a 1k prompt validation set. No extraneous text allowed outside the top-level JSON object.
- Tool/function calling: explicit, auditable invocations where the model returns a top-level array of actions like:
  - {"tool": "create_order", "args": { ... }}
- Deterministic formatting: validators must be able to parse responses without heuristics; failure mode should be a clear validation error rather than silent parsing.
- Observability: per-invocation logs (tool name, args, model response, timestamp) retained for 90 days and surfaced in Console.
- Latency target: enforcing structured output should add <=150ms p99 to median inference time for our target prompt shapes.

What we prototyped / recommended in-call
- Function-calling-first approach: instruct the model to return a single top-level JSON payload (no surrounding commentary).
- A strict JSON schema that includes an "actions" array of objects with schema for "tool" (string), "args" (object), and an optional "metadata" block.
- Kernel-level validations + fallback policy: if schema fails, return an explicit error object so orchestrator can decide retry vs human review.

Attachments
- redwood-draft-json-schema-v1.json (attached) — first pass schema for the responses we discussed
- redwood-agent-workflow-diagram.png (attached) — suggested agent orchestration with pre-check -> tool-invoke -> post-check loop

Next steps (mutual action items)
1) We (Redwood) to share the Draft JSON schema (attached) and a short demo showing: a) model enforcing the schema, b) tool call logs, c) failure mode handling — target: this week (by Fri, Mar 6).
2) You (Aster) to run the attached validator on a representative prompt set and share failure examples / edge cases (due: Mon, Mar 9).
3) Technical deep dive: 60-min session with your platform engineers + our runtime team to walk through integration options (function calling vs companion tools) — propose Wed, Mar 11 @ 10am PT.
4) We will provide an initial QPS / cost estimate for a 6-week PoC and a sample SLA for dedicated capacity (estimated item in attached PoC spreadsheet).

If that aligns, I’ll book the deep dive and loop in our runtime engineer (Marissa) and solutions lead (Lauren).

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0182

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured JSON output requirements

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear write-up, this is exactly the format we like. A few clarifications from our side:

- Security/compliance: we need to ensure that any tool invocation payloads never contain PHI and that logs are redacted or stored under customer-controlled KMS. Can you confirm Redwood's approach for KMS/HSM integration and log redaction?
- Schema: the attached looks like a good starting point. Two things to check: a) we need strong typing for "args" (specific fields for order creation vs update), and b) a validation mode that returns a machine-readable error code we can map to our orchestrator.
- Timeline & scale: for the PoC we expect ~100 QPS bursty, steady-state ~10 QPS. Can you include cost/latency estimates for both Hosted and Dedicated options?

Action items for us: we’ll run your schema against ~500 representative prompts (security-scrubbed) and return examples of failures by Mon, Mar 9. We’ll also confirm who from our infra team will join the deep dive.

One more ask: can Redwood provide a short sample of how the tool call audit log looks (example lines) and the retention/exports? That will help our compliance team.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the demo.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | Aster Health
samir.patel@asterhealth.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@asterhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured JSON output requirements

Samir —

Appreciate the quick reply and the compliance note — agree that KMS integration and log redaction are must-haves. Quick responses to your points: 

- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for log encryption and can integrate with your AWS KMS; we can scope an HSM-backed option for Dedicated/Private deployments. I’ll have Marissa follow up with specific integration steps and docs before the deep dive.
- Typed args & machine errors: the schema we attached is intentionally generic for the discovery phase. For the PoC we’ll produce typed sub-schemas for each tool (create_order, update_order, cancel_order) and include a machine-readable error specification (error_code, field, reason).
- Scale & pricing: we’ll include Hosted vs Dedicated cost and latency tables in the PoC estimate. Early note: 100 QPS burst is well within Dedicated capacity plans; Hosted can handle it but pricing will differ — we’ll call that out.
- Audit log sample: see inline example below (we will also attach a log export sample in the PoC package):

[EXAMPLE LOG LINE]
2026-03-05T21:55:12Z | request_id=abc123 | model=gpt-XX | tool=create_order | args={"order_id":"ORD-4752","amount":123.45} | response_schema=PASS | latency_ms=138

Next steps: I’ll schedule the deep dive for Wed, Mar 11 @ 10am PT and share calendar invites. Marissa will surface the KMS integration doc and a more detailed typed-schema draft by Fri. I’ll also add a short sample log export and an example error-code mapping in the PoC folder.

If Lauren or Marissa want anything else on the invite, flag now.

Thanks,

Jordan
